scams.name: The SSA Coopataxi Kiosk
scams.description:
Salvador Bahia (SSA) is North-East Brazil's second-busiest airport after Recife, sitting 28 kilometers north of Pelourinho via the BR-324 and BA-526 access roads. The airport has Uber, 99, and InDriver coverage with reasonable supply during the day but documented thinner driver availability after 10pm — and that thinness is the lever for the most consistent SSA arrivals trap, where unauthorized drivers wait near the Aplicativos pickup zone for travelers whose Uber matches drop and offer "cash only" rides at three to five times the app rate. The trap economy follows the Brazilian-airport template: "Special Taxi" kiosks selling fixed-rate quotes well above metered fare, sign-holders posing as "pousada transfer" agents inside arrivals, and credit-card cloning at unofficial cooperative counters.

The trap menu has seven recurring mechanics. "Special Taxi" or Coopataxi kiosks inside SSA arrivals quote R$200–R$400 to Barra, Pelourinho, or Rio Vermelho against an Uber rate of R$70–R$130. Sign-holders posing as "pousada transfer" agents intercept tourists in the baggage hall (legitimate hotel transfers wait outside arrivals with a printed name). Uber cancel-and-recontract works the post-22:00 thin-supply window — the in-app driver cancels, an unauthorized driver appears with a cash quote, and the traveler defaults to that out of fatigue. "Meter broken" yellow-taxi demands materialize at hotel arrival with a R$250+ flat-rate cash demand. "Overnight surcharge R$80" added unannounced after late-night arrivals isn't a legitimate fee. Credit-card cloning at unofficial cooperative counters via "manual entry" card-machines is the most damaging variant — the card details get skimmed during a transaction that itself isn't fraud. During Carnaval (February through March), legitimate prices spike three to five times and trap quotes spike correspondingly. Real fares anchor at R$80–R$130 to Pelourinho, R$70–R$110 to Barra, R$70–R$120 to Rio Vermelho, with 35–60 minute travel times.

Book Uber, 99, or InDriver on airport Wi-Fi after collecting your luggage — expect R$80–R$130 to Pelourinho, R$70–R$110 to Barra, R$70–R$120 to Rio Vermelho. Meet your driver at the signposted Aplicativos pickup zone at the terminal exit. Refuse every "Special Taxi" kiosk quoting R$180+, every sign-holding "pousada transfer" agent inside arrivals, every "meter broken" R$250 cash demand at the hotel, every "overnight surcharge R$80" against the regulated rate, and every "manual entry" credit-card transaction at unofficial cooperative counters. For late-night arrivals after 10pm, the R$15–R$30 surcharge for Uber Comfort or 99 Top buys a more reliable driver and is worth it; allow 10–20 minutes of wait time when supply is thin. Pay in-app or cash only — never hand a credit card to any taxi driver. For Carnaval, budget three to five times normal taxi rates and book Uber Black or pre-arrange hotel transfer. Get a Brazilian eSIM (Vivo, Claro, TIM) for guaranteed connectivity before relying on Uber. Save DEATUR Salvador +55 71 3116 6817 (English available, Praça da Sé) and US Consulate Recife +55 81 3416 3050 (covers Bahia) before arrival.
scams.avoidance: Book Uber, 99, or InDriver on airport Wi-Fi — SSA to Pelourinho R$80–R$130. For late-night (post-10pm), pay R$15–R$30 surcharge for Uber Comfort or 99 Top. Ignore "Special Taxi" kiosks quoting above R$180. Don't hand a credit card to any taxi driver — pay in-app or cash only. DEATUR Salvador +55 71 3116 6817 (English available, Praça da Sé).
scams.location: Salvador Bahia Airport (SSA) arrivals halls (Terminals 1 & 2), 'Special Taxi' kiosks, Cocobambu / Coopataxi counters, Barra / Pelourinho / Itapuã drop-offs
scams.tldr: A "Special Taxi" or Coopataxi kiosk inside SSA arrivals quotes R$320 to your Pelourinho pousada while you're jet-lagged and dragging luggage. The real Uber fare is R$70–R$130. After 10pm, driver supply thins and unauthorized cash-only drivers approach Aplicativos passengers whose rides have dropped.

scams.name: The Pelourinho Fita Ribbon
scams.description:
The "Fita do Senhor do Bonfim" (Bonfim ribbon) is a genuine Bahian Catholic-Candomblé blessing ribbon — colorful printed silk strips sold at the actual Igreja do Senhor do Bonfim church on Praia do Bonfim and at every Pelourinho gift shop for R$0.50–R$2 each, often in packs of 12 for R$6–R$18. The ribbon is tied around the wrist with three knots, each representing a wish that comes true when the ribbon eventually breaks. That genuine tradition is the cover story for the most common Pelourinho forced-tip scam, which targets obvious tourists (cameras, English-speaking, hotel-zone clothes) on the cobblestone streets between Largo do Pelourinho and Praça da Sé.

The mechanic has four stages and several variants. Stage one: a friendly local approaches with "free fita do Bonfim, three wishes" framing on the cobblestones. Stage two: before you can decline meaningfully, the ribbon is tied with three knots around your wrist. Stage three: a R$20–R$100 "donation" demand once the ribbon is on, against the R$0.50–R$2 church-shop price. Stage four: refusal escalates to verbal pressure, accusations of disrespect, or "bad luck if you remove the blessing." The same coordinated forced-tip ecosystem runs three other scripts. The Bahiana-photo variant: a costumed white-dress Baiana woman appears in your line of sight, you take an unsolicited photo, then a R$50 "photo for charity" or "Pelourinho cultural fund" demand lands. The capoeira-roda variant: tourists watch a 5-minute street capoeira performance, then face a R$50 demand when legitimate street rodas are tip-based at R$5–R$20 voluntary. The street-artist variant: a "quick caricature R$30" becomes R$150 "frame plus delivery" once the drawing is done. All four target the same impulse compassion and the same English-language vulnerability.

Refuse every "free fita" or "free blessing" offer on the Pelourinho cobblestones — there is no legitimate free fita, and the R$20–R$100 "donation" that follows is the trap. If you want a Bonfim ribbon, buy direct at the Igreja do Senhor do Bonfim gift shop on Praia do Bonfim at R$0.50–R$2 each (or packs of 12 for R$6–R$18). Say "não, obrigado" firmly to every "free" photo with a Bahiana, every street capoeira approach, and every "quick caricature" offer in Pelourinho. The legitimate paid capoeira show is at Forte da Capoeira on Largo do Santo Antônio at R$30–R$50 with no surprise charges, and street rodas are tip-based at R$5–R$20 voluntary. For photos with the iconic white-dress Baiana figures, agree the price before the photo (R$5–R$10 per photo is fair for the professional models who pose for tourists). Pelourinho is broadly safe for daytime sightseeing, but the cobblestone narrow streets concentrate the forced-tip touts — visit 9am–5pm on weekdays and avoid evenings when vendors are more aggressive. DEATUR Salvador +55 71 3116 6817 sits at Praça da Sé for incident reports.
scams.avoidance: Buy fita at the official Igreja do Senhor do Bonfim gift shop at R$0.50–R$2 each. Firm "não obrigado" to every Pelourinho "free" offer. Capoeira: Forte da Capoeira paid show R$30–R$50; street rodas tip-based R$5–R$20. For Bahiana photos, agree R$5–R$10 before the shutter clicks. Visit Pelourinho daytime only (9am–5pm weekdays); DEATUR +55 71 3116 6817.
scams.location: Pelourinho cobblestone streets (Largo do Pelourinho, Terreiro de Jesus), Igreja do Senhor do Bonfim church area (Itapagipe peninsula), Mercado Modelo, walking-tour pickup zones
scams.tldr: A friendly local on the Pelourinho cobblestones offers a "free fita do Bonfim, three wishes," ties three knots around your wrist before you can decline, and follows with a R$50 "donation" demand. The same ribbon costs R$0.50–R$2 at the actual Bonfim church gift shop. Variants run unsolicited Bahiana photos, capoeira-roda donations, and R$150 caricature frames.

scams.name: The Pelourinho Crowd Pickpocket
scams.description:
Pelourinho is Salvador's UNESCO colonial old town and the cultural heart of Afro-Brazilian Bahia — unmissable for tourists drawn by the cobblestone streets, the São Francisco Church gilded interior, the Largo do Pelourinho UNESCO core, the Casa de Jorge Amado, and the Pelourinho Carnival Museum. That same density of camera-ready visitors makes it the city's highest-density pickpocket-team operating zone, with organized 3–5 member crews working the same template flagged in São Paulo's Centro pickpocket reports and Salvador's own 2025 traveler-safety threads. The pattern is heavy enough that a community warning has surfaced about specific tour operators (notably Olafemi Tours) booking Pelourinho walks with insufficient security awareness.

There are nine specific risk zones with predictable mechanics. Pelourinho organized teams target tourists photographing cobblestone streets, São Francisco Church, and Largo do Pelourinho with distraction-theft templates. Mercado Modelo plaza absorbs phone-snatches from outdoor café tables. The Elevador Lacerda art-deco lift connecting Cidade Baixa to Cidade Alta has narrow boarding queues that funnel tourists into team-pickpocket setups. Praça da Sé and the Cathedral approach see "helpful local" direction-givers paired with bag-watchers. Capoeira-roda crowds get worked at the watching-tourist edge of the circle during performances. The Mercado Modelo artisan-market interior runs distraction-team brush-pasts in the narrow stall aisles. Sunset on Praça da Sé sees phone-snatches with sprinting into the descending Pelourinho streets where chasing is impossible. The "are you Spanish?" confusion approach is the conversational variant — a stranger asks about a country you didn't claim, while a partner moves in. Olafemi Tours specifically is flagged in r/Brazil 2025 community warnings for walking-tour operators who don't enforce body-positioned-bag posture among guests. Night-time Pelourinho post-7pm is significantly less safe than daytime, and most documented theft happens in the after-dark colonial-zone narrow streets.

Visit Pelourinho daytime only (9am–5pm, weekdays preferred over weekends), wear a zipped crossbody bag in front and keep your phone in a zipped inner pocket between uses, take Uber or 99 between Pelourinho and your hotel rather than walking, avoid Pelourinho after 7pm unless going directly to a reserved-table restaurant via Uber drop-off, and refuse every "helpful local" direction approach, every "are you Spanish?" conversational opener, and every photo-help offer in cobblestone-street density. Bring nothing you can't afford to lose — leave passport, jewelry, and valuable watches in the hotel safe. Use the phone selfie timer or ask security guards or hotel staff for photos rather than handing your phone to a stranger. Book walking tours only through Google 4.5+ operators with 50+ reviews — Cláudio's Walking Tour Pelourinho, Salvador Bahia Tours, and Free Walker Tour Salvador are reputable — and avoid Olafemi Tours per the 2025 community warning. DEATUR Salvador +55 71 3116 6817 sits at Praça da Sé inside Pelourinho — file a Boletim de Ocorrência within 24 hours of any incident for insurance and chargeback evidence.
scams.avoidance: Visit Pelourinho daytime only, 9am–5pm on weekdays preferred. Leave valuables in the hotel safe; carry a zipped crossbody bag worn in front. Phone in a zipped front pocket between uses; never on outdoor café tables. Take Uber or 99 between Pelourinho and your hotel; avoid walking after 7pm. Reputable walking tours: Cláudio's, Salvador Bahia Tours, Free Walker Tour Salvador.
scams.location: Pelourinho cobblestone streets (Largo do Pelourinho, Terreiro de Jesus, Largo do Cruzeiro de São Francisco), Mercado Modelo plaza, Elevador Lacerda upper plaza, Praça da Sé / Cathedral approach
scams.tldr: Pelourinho (Salvador's UNESCO colonial old town) hosts the city's highest-density pickpocket ring — organized 3–5 member teams target photographers around São Francisco Church and Largo do Pelourinho, the Mercado Modelo and Elevador Lacerda boarding queues funnel tourists into team setups, and capoeira-roda crowds get worked from the edges. Visit daytime-only weekdays, never walk after 7pm.

scams.name: The Morro de São Paulo Catamarã
scams.description:
Morro de São Paulo is Bahia's signature beach day-trip and overnight escape — a car-free island village 60 kilometers south of Salvador, reached only by sea via two-hour fast-boat from Mercado Modelo / Comércio pier in Salvador. Three reputable catamarã operators with Marinha registration run the route: Biotur, Ilha Bela, and Cassi Tour, with three to four daily departures and round-trip pricing of R$130–R$220 per person. The island village itself is walkable end-to-end in 20 minutes, with four numbered praias (Primeira through Quarta and an outer Quinta Praia) reachable on foot or via beach-hopping mini-schooners from the main pier at R$50–R$100. A R$35 environmental conservation tax is mandatory and legitimate at island arrival; everything above that is a markup target.

The trap menu has eight recurring mechanics. Pelourinho tour-booking touts sell "private speedboat to Morro R$800 per person" against the legitimate catamarã round-trip at R$130–R$220 — the "private" speedboat usually doesn't materialize as advertised. Hotel-concierge "all-inclusive Morro day-trip + lunch + return R$600 per person" against a real DIY of R$325–R$415 (catamarã R$130–R$220 + R$35 tax + R$80 lunch + R$80 schooner). "VIP exclusive route to Quarta Praia + Quinta Praia R$1,200" charges for stops already on every standard beach-hopping itinerary. "Mandatory island guide R$200" on Morro is fictional — the village is small enough to walk in 20 minutes and no guide is required anywhere. Unlicensed catamarãs without life jackets or Marinha registration carry real safety risk on the Bahia coast in summer-storm season, and the "cheap R$80 catamarã today" offer at the pier is the warning sign. The conservation tax gets inflated from R$35 to R$100+ at island arrival by counterfeit booth operators (always pay at the official booth and keep the receipt). Olafemi Tours surfaces here too with poor logistics on Morro packages per r/Brazil 2025 warnings. And a "Boipeba island add-on R$400" bundles a separate 2-hour boat trip south of Morro into the Salvador-side package when Boipeba's actual day-trip from Morro pier is R$80–R$150.

Book the catamarã direct at the Mercado Modelo / Comércio pier ticket window — Biotur, Ilha Bela, or Cassi Tour at R$130–R$220 round-trip per person. Verify life jackets and the Marinha registration sticker before boarding. Pay the legitimate R$35 environmental conservation tax at the official island booth on arrival (keep the receipt, refuse any R$100+ demand). Book beach-hopping schooners directly at the Morro main pier at R$50–R$100, and refuse every "private speedboat R$800," "all-inclusive day-trip R$600," "VIP exclusive route R$1,200," "mandatory island guide R$200," and "Boipeba add-on R$400" upsell from Salvador-side operators. Overnighting in Morro for one to two nights is much better than a same-day day-trip — same-day return is rushed at four hours of boats plus four to five hours on the island. Reputable Morro pousadas include Pousada Vila do Mar, Anima Hotel, and Pousada Catavento. The village has no cars; for travelers with mobility concerns the "tractor taxi" (open-air tractor-pulled cart) is R$10–R$20 to most pousadas. Take Dramamine 30 minutes before catamarã departure — the open ocean can be rough December–February. Avoid Olafemi Tours per the community warning; DEATUR Salvador +55 71 3116 6817 takes incident reports.
scams.avoidance: Book the catamarã direct at Mercado Modelo pier: Biotur, Ilha Bela, or Cassi at R$130–R$220. Verify life jackets and Marinha registration before boarding. Pay R$35 conservation tax at the official island booth and keep the receipt. Beach-hopping schooner direct from Morro main pier R$50–R$100. Overnight one to two nights in Morro — better than a rushed day-trip.
scams.location: Salvador Mercado Modelo / Comércio fast-boat pier (Catamarã do Morro), Pelourinho tour-booking touts, hotel-concierge day-trip desks, Morro de São Paulo arrival pier
scams.tldr: Morro de São Paulo is Bahia's flagship car-free island village 60 km south of Salvador. The legitimate route is R$130–R$220 round-trip via Biotur, Ilha Bela, or Cassi Tour catamarãs from Mercado Modelo pier, plus a R$35 conservation tax on arrival. Pelourinho touts sell "private speedboat R$800" and hotel concierges bundle "all-inclusive day-trip R$600" against a real DIY of R$325–R$415.

scams.name: The Pelourinho Bossa Nova Couvert
scams.description:
Salvador's three main dining strips — the Pelourinho colonial cobblestone, the Rio Vermelho bohemian district, and the Barra waterfront — concentrate the city's tourist-facing restaurant scene and run the standard Brazilian-coastal-city couvert-and-serviço bill-padding pattern flagged in Recife, Maceió, and Fortaleza. Brazilian consumer law (Lei 13.419/2017) makes the 10% serviço charge explicitly optional, INMETRO regulates pricing disclosure, and PROCON Bahia enforces against double-charging — but the disclosure obligation is routinely buried in fine print at tourist-strip venues, especially the Pelourinho cobblestone restaurants pitched at cruise-day visitors and Carnaval-week travelers.

The trap menu has ten recurring mechanics. USD-only menus on the Pelourinho cobblestone strip price Bahian moqueca de peixe at US$35+ when the same dish is R$80–R$130 at non-tourist spots. "Couvert artístico" is layered at R$25–R$80 per person for a single guitarist or a 5-minute capoeira show when legitimate couvert for a real performer is R$10–R$25 disclosed before seating. "Serviço 13–15%" replaces the standard optional 10%. "Taxa de couvert + serviço" double-charging is illegal per PROCON BA but appears regularly. Bottled "água mineral R$18" replaces the real R$5–R$10. "Caipirinha de cachaça artesanal premium R$50" is poured from house cachaça at R$18–R$30. "Lagosta peso variável" market-price lobster at R$800–R$1,400 per kg without disclosed weight is the most expensive single line item. Bill-switcheroo where the printed receipt differs from the card-charge by R$50–R$200 is the closing variant. Mercado Modelo upstairs tourist-restaurants serve touristy adaptations of Bahian classics at twice working-class prices. And Rio Vermelho "live samba serenade" surcharges land at R$100 per person added during the meal without prior disclosure.

Eat at authentic Bahian spots — Restaurante Maria Mata Mouro on Largo do Cruzeiro de São Francisco (Google 4.6+, R$100–R$250), Casa de Tereza in Rio Vermelho (traditional Bahian, R$90–R$200), Mistura in Rio Vermelho (contemporary Bahian, R$120–R$280), Boteco do França on Largo do Pelourinho (casual Bahian, R$60–R$140), or licensed Baiana street vendors for acarajé at R$12–R$25. Before sitting, photograph the menu, confirm couvert artístico amount per person and serviço policy and credit-card surcharge in writing, refuse every unordered couvert with "eu não pedi," agree weight in writing for any "lagosta peso variável" or fish platter (fair lobster R$400–R$700 per kg), and refuse the 10% serviço if service is poor since Lei 13.419/2017 makes it optional. Order "água sem gás copo" (free tap water) rather than the bottled R$18 markup. Caipirinhas should be R$18–R$30 at reputable Bahian spots — anything above R$50 is tourist-trap pricing. Moqueca's fair price at authentic spots is R$80–R$180 per person; R$250+ is the tourist-trap mark. Acarajé from licensed Baiana street vendors (with the cebola painted on the stand) at Rio Vermelho or Largo da Mariquita is the right answer at R$12–R$25 each, not the R$50 "tourist menu" version. Refuse the R$100 "live samba serenade" surcharge if it wasn't disclosed before. PROCON BA can be contacted via 151 or procon.ba.gov.br for any abusive bill.
scams.avoidance: Reputable Salvador picks: Maria Mata Mouro, Casa de Tereza, Mistura, Boteco do França. Acarajé da Cira (Rio Vermelho street vendor) at R$12–R$25 each. Before sitting, photograph the menu and confirm couvert + serviço + card surcharge in writing. "Serviço" is optional under Lei 13.419/2017 — refuse if poor service. PROCON BA: 151 or procon.ba.gov.br for abusive bills.
scams.location: Pelourinho restaurant strip (Largo do Pelourinho, Rua das Laranjeiras), Rio Vermelho bohemian dining strip (Largo da Mariquita), Barra waterfront restaurants, Mercado Modelo upstairs restaurants
scams.tldr: Pelourinho cobblestone-strip restaurants post USD-only menus at 2–3× local prices (Bahian moqueca de peixe at US$35+ vs R$80–R$130 at non-tourist spots), layer R$25–R$80 "couvert artístico" for a single guitarist or 5-minute capoeira show, and charge "serviço 13–15%" against the optional 10% standard. Brazilian Lei 13.419/2017 makes serviço optional and you can refuse.

scams.name: The Salvador Camarote Counterfeit
scams.description:
Salvador hosts the world's largest Carnaval street party — a four-to-seven-day February event with 2.5 million daily participants spread across three trio elétrico circuits (Barra–Ondina, Campo Grande–Praça Castro Alves, and Pelourinho), running on a scale that drives accommodation rates and Camarote (elevated VIP balcony) tickets five to ten times normal pricing. That scale and price pressure creates exactly the same cancel-and-relist booking fraud, WhatsApp PIX-upfront apartment scam, and counterfeit-ticket reselling pattern that mirrors Rio Carnaval and Recife/Olinda — plus a Salvador-specific "Abadá" (bloco T-shirt) counterfeit market for the color-coded shirts that grant access to a specific bloco's roped-off circle on the trio elétrico route.

The trap menu has eight recurring patterns. Booking.com and Airbnb phantom listings use stolen photos of properties that don't exist or are already booked; you pay in advance and arrive to find nothing. Confirmed bookings get cancelled 30–60 days before Carnaval and re-listed at five to ten times the original price. WhatsApp "private Barra apartment for Carnaval R$6,000/night" demands 100% PIX upfront — Brazilian PIX is irreversible, and the listing disappears the moment payment confirms. Unauthorized resellers sell "Camarote VIP ticket R$4,000" against legitimate prices of R$1,500–R$5,000 from the official venue websites Camarote Salvador (camarotesalvador.com.br), Camarote Expresso 2222 (camaroteexpresso2222.com.br), and Camarote Andar do Mar. "Abadá" counterfeits sell at R$600–R$2,000 from unauthorized resellers when each bloco's official website (Bloco do Bell, Banda Eva, Daniela Mercury, Ivete Sangalo, Cheiro de Amor, Saulo, Bell Marques) sells the legitimate shirt at R$400–R$2,500 — and counterfeits scan invalid at the bloco-rope checkpoint on the trio elétrico route. On-arrival bait-and-switch downgrades a confirmed beachfront unit to an inferior room. "Cleaning deposit R$800 cash on arrival" never returns at checkout. And "mandatory Carnaval pousada package R$8,000 for 5 nights" inflates five times the normal nightly rate.

Book Salvador Carnaval 9–12 months ahead via Booking.com or established hotel chains with platform-protected card payment — Wish Hotel da Bahia at Campo Grande (central to Carnaval circuits), Pestana Convento do Carmo (boutique), Fera Palace Hotel, or Bahia Othon Palace (Ondina circuit beachfront) — never PIX-transfer to a WhatsApp "apartment" seller. Buy Camarote VIP tickets only at camaroteexpresso2222.com.br or camarotesalvador.com.br at R$1,500–R$5,000, buy Abadá bloco T-shirts only from each bloco's official website at R$400–R$2,500, and refuse every "private reseller Camarote R$4,000," every "Abadá R$600–R$2,000" from an unauthorized seller as counterfeit, and every on-arrival "cleaning deposit R$800 cash" demand and "mandatory Carnaval package R$8,000" upsell. Avoid Airbnb for peak-season Carnaval entirely (cancel-and-relist is documented across Brazil). Cross-reference any pousada or Camarote on Google Maps and Tripadvisor before booking. The chão / pipoca crowd of 2.5 million daily participants is intense and pickpocket risk is high — paying for an elevated Camarote (food, drink, restroom, security) is the safest way for older travelers. For budget Carnaval, base at Lauro de Freitas 20 km north of Centro and Uber into the circuits at half the Barra/Ondina rate. DEATUR Salvador +55 71 3116 6817 takes booking-fraud denuncias within 48 hours.
scams.avoidance: Book Salvador Carnaval 9–12 months ahead via Booking.com or hotel chains. Reputable picks: Wish Hotel da Bahia, Pestana Convento do Carmo, Fera Palace, Bahia Othon. Camarote tickets only from camaroteexpresso2222.com.br or camarotesalvador.com.br. Abadá only from each bloco's official website (Bloco do Bell, Banda Eva, Cheiro de Amor). For budget Carnaval, base at Lauro de Freitas (20 km north) and Uber into the circuits.
scams.location: Salvador Carnaval circuits (Barra-Ondina, Campo Grande, Pelourinho), Camarote VIP venues, online ticket resellers, hotel-concierge Carnaval-package bookings, WhatsApp 'private apartment' Carnaval rentals
scams.tldr: Salvador Carnaval (the world's largest street party with 2.5 million daily participants over 4–7 days in February) drives accommodation and ticket prices 5–10× normal. R$4,000 "Camarote VIP" tickets resell against R$1,500–R$5,000 official prices from camarotesalvador.com.br and camaroteexpresso2222.com.br, and counterfeit "Abadá" bloco T-shirts at R$600–R$2,000 scan invalid at the bloco-rope checkpoint.
